title: aaa_diameter Module
content_markdown:
This module provides an RFC 6733 Diameter peer implementation, being able to act as either **Diameter client** or **server**, or **both**.

Any module that wishes to use it has to do the following:

*   _include aaa.h_
    
*   _make a bind call with a proper Diameter-specific URL, e.g. "diameter:freeDiameter-client.conf"_
overview:
This module provides an RFC 6733 Diameter peer implementation, being able to act as either **Diameter client** or **server**, or **both**.

Any module that wishes to use it has to do the following:

*   _include aaa.h_
    
*   _make a bind call with a proper Diameter-specific URL, e.g. "diameter:freeDiameter-client.conf"_
how_it_works:
The module implements the core AAA OpenSIPS interface, thus offering an alternative client implementation to the [aaa_radius](aaa_radius) module which can be useful, for example, when performing billing and accounting for the live SIP calls.

In addition to the RADIUS client's auth and accounting features, the Diameter client includes support for sending _arbitrary_ Diameter requests, further opening up the scope of applications which can be achieved through OpenSIPS scripting. Such Diameter requests can be sent using the [dm_send_request()](#func_dm_send_request "1.6.1.� dm_send_request(app_id, cmd_code, avps_json, [rpl_avps_pv])") function.

Starting with OpenSIPS **3.5**, the Diameter module includes _server-side_ support as well.

First, the [event_route](event_route) module must be loaded in order to be able to process [E_DM_REQUEST](#event_dm_request "1.8.1.� E_DM_REQUEST") events in the OpenSIPS configuration file. These events will contain all necessary information on the incoming Diameter request.

Finally, once the request information is processed and the answer AVPs are prepared, script writers should use the [dm_send_answer()](#func_dm_send_answer "1.6.2.� dm_send_answer(avps_json, [is_error])") function in order to reply with a Diameter answer message.

_Recommendation:_ When possible, always load the **dict_sip.fdx** freeDiameter extension module inside your _freeDiameter.conf_ configuration file, as it contains hundreds of well-known AVP definitions which may be good to have when inter-operating with other Diameter peer implementations.

dependencies_required.name: libfdcore
dependencies_required.reason: Diameter message building, parsing, peer state machine and network communication (v1.2.1 or higher)

dependencies_required.name: libfdproto
dependencies_required.reason: Diameter message building, parsing, peer state machine and network communication (v1.2.1 or higher)

exported_parameters.name: fd_log_level
exported_parameters.description: This parameter measures the quietness of the logging done by the freeDiameter library.
exported_parameters.notes: NOTE: since freeDiameter logs to standard output, you must also enable the new core parameter, log_stdout, before getting any logs from the library.

exported_parameters.name: realm
exported_parameters.description: The unique realm to be used by all participating Diameter peers.

exported_parameters.name: peer_identity
exported_parameters.description: The identity (realm subdomain) of the Diameter server peer, to which the OpenSIPS Diameter client peer will connect.

exported_parameters.name: aaa_url
exported_parameters.description: URL of the diameter client: the configuration file, with an optional extra-avps-file, where the Diameter client is configured. By default, the connection is not created.

exported_parameters.name: answer_timeout
exported_parameters.description: Time, in milliseconds, after which a dm_send_request() function call with no received reply will time out and return a -2 code.

exported_parameters.name: max_json_log_size
exported_parameters.description: When an error log is printed due to malformed JSON, this parameter indicates how many characters from the JSON should be printed at console. A higher value might overcrowd the logs, but can be useful for troubleshooting.

exported_functions.name: dm_send_request

parameters.name: app_id
parameters.description: ID of the application. A custom application must be defined in the dictionary.opensips Diameter configuration file before it can be recognized.

parameters.name: cmd_code
parameters.description: ID of the command. A custom command code, name and AVP requirements must be defined in the dictionary.opensips Diameter configuration file beforehand. body of the HTTP response.

parameters.name: avps_json
parameters.description: A JSON Array containing the AVPs to include in the message.

parameters.name: rpl_avps_pv
parameters.description: output variable which will hold all AVP names from the Diameter Answer along with their values, packed as a JSON Array string. The "json" module and its _$json_ variable could be used to iterate this array.

return_values.condition: Request timeout (the answer_timeout was exceeded before an Answer could be processed)

exported_functions.description: Perform a blocking Diameter request over to the interconnected peer and return the Result-Code AVP value from the reply.

# Requests and Replies in the "dictionary.opensips" file

ATTRIBUTE out_gw            232 string
ATTRIBUTE trunk_id          233 string

ATTRIBUTE call_cost         235 integer

ATTRIBUTE Exponent          429 integer32
ATTRIBUTE Value-Digits      447 integer64

ATTRIBUTE Cost-Unit 424 grouped
{
	Value-Digits | REQUIRED | 1

exported_functions.name: dm_send_answer

parameters.name: avps_json
parameters.description: A JSON Array containing the AVPs to include in the answer message (example below).

parameters.name: is_error
parameters.description: Set to true in order to set the 'E' (error) bit in the answer message.

exported_functions.description:
Send back a Diameter answer message to the interconnected peer in a _non-blocking_ fashion, in response to its request.

The following fields will be automatically copied over from the Diameter request when building the answer message:

*   Application ID
*   Command Code
*   Session-Id AVP, if any
*   Transaction-Id AVP, if any (only applies when Session-Id is not present)

exported_events.name: E_DM_REQUEST
exported_events.description: This event is raised whenever the _aaa_diameter_ module is loaded and OpenSIPS receives a Diameter request on the configured Diameter listening interface.

parameters.name: sess_id
parameters.description: the value of either the _Session-Id_ AVP, _Transaction-Id_ AVP or a _NULL_ value if neither of these transaction-identifying AVPs is present in the Diameter request.

parameters.name: avps_json
parameters.description: a JSON Array containing the AVPs of the request. Use the [json](json) module's **$json** variable to easily parse and work with it.

exported_events.subscribe_method: Mainly consumed by an event_route, but can be consumed through any other EVI-compatible delivery channel.

configuration_examples.title: `dm_send_request` usage
configuration_examples.code:
\# Building an sending an My-Custom-Request (92001) for the
# My Diameter Application (42)
$var(payload) = "\[
	{ \"Origin-Host\": \"client.diameter.test\" },
	{ \"Origin-Realm\": \"diameter.test\" },
	{ \"Destination-Realm\": \"diameter.test\" },
	{ \"Sip-From-Tag\": \"dc93-4fba-91db\" },
	{ \"Sip-To-Tag\": \"ae12-47d6-816a\" },
	{ \"Session-Id\": \"a59c-dff0d9efd167\" },
	{ \"Sip-Call-Duration\": 6 },
	{ \"Sip-Call-Setuptime\": 1 },
	{ \"Sip-Call-Created\": 1652372541 },
	{ \"Sip-Call-MSDuration\": 5850 },
	{ \"out\_gw\": \"GW-774\" },
	{ \"call\_cost\": 10 },
	{ \"Cost-Information\": \[
		{\"Unit-Value\": \[{\"Value-Digits\": 1000}\]},
		{\"Currency-Code\": 35}
		\]}
\]";

$var(rc) = dm\_send\_request(42, 92001, $var(payload), $var(rpl\_avps));
xlog("rc: $var(rc), AVPs: $var(rpl\_avps)\n");
$json(avps) := $var(rpl\_avps);
